profile_text.body:
Cerence Inc. describes itself as "Cerence AI | AI for a World in Motion," delivering conversational and agentic AI-powered user experiences for automotive and beyond. The company says its work is powered by CaLLM, which it describes as an advanced family of language models, and brings conversational AI to the automotive world and beyond, enabling natural, multimodal, and safe interactions. Its site also discusses AI for automotive dealerships, industrial AI, and in-car voice AI.

The company highlights Cerence Emergency Vehicle Detection (EVD), which it says is already deployed in production vehicles. EVD uses existing vehicle microphones and AI trained to distinguish sirens from traffic, road noise, music, and other sounds. Cerence states the system can detect and localize more than 1,500 emergency sirens across nearly 50 countries, identify approaching emergency vehicles from more than 300 meters away with interior microphones, and beyond 800 meters when paired with exterior microphones. Cerence also reports third quarter results with revenue up 12% YoY, connected services revenue up 20% YoY, and operating cash flow of $20M supporting a first-ever share repurchase program. The site includes discussion of Zero Trust Architecture with Microsoft, naming Kaivan Karimi and Frank Kaleck.

Cerence Inc. is a public company headquartered in Burlington, Massachusetts, trading under the ticker CRNC, with SEC CIK 0001768267. A Massachusetts legal exposure listing shows 191 entries for the company. The company is also listed as CERENCE INC.
